title.narrative: Strategic Partnership 2019-2023

description.narrative: Multiannual strategic partnership between the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Government of the Netherlands and the International Crisis Group (CG) which supports CG in its mission of global conflict prevention and resolution activities. The partnership provides the MFA with valued activities in priority conflict situations within the MFA’s result framework.

recipient-region.narrative: Crisis Group’s provides analysis and advice on how to prevent, resolve or better manage deadly conflict through independent research, concrete policy prescriptions for conflict prevention and by shaping the international debate. The Strategic Partnership 2019-2023 between the MFA and International Crisis Group consists of two components: Core support to Crisis Group's conflict prevention and resolution activities and earmarked support of the Government of the Netherlands for engagement on a range of priority conflicts and Early Warning for certain priority contexts.

title.narrative: International Crisis Group Core Report of Activities and Impact 2022-2023

description.narrative: This Core Report describes how Crisis Group has helped inform and influence policymakers, armed groups, civil society organisations and others for the purpose of preventing, mitigating and resolving deadly conflict. It showcases how, through a combination of on-the-ground research and high-level advocacy, we have delivered on our priorities from 1 July 2022 to 30 June 2023.

title.narrative: Ongoing media outreach, including through social media.

description.narrative: Crisis Group’s public profile has grown steadily since the start of the partnership in 2019. For example, Crisis Group's website views increased drastically from 2016/2017 to 2022/2023, from 2.3 million to 5.7 million views respectively, almost tripling the number of views. The organization's social media content creation amplified Crisis Group’s reach.

title.narrative: Number of website page views

comment.narrative: Crisis Group’s public profile was strong with 6,1 million website views and our Twitter impressions reached 33.4 million. This year, in another effort to adapt to the changing social media landscape, Crisis Group began producing Reels on Instagram. On Instagram, our first Reels, or short format videos, featuring our Europe and Central Asia program director and senior Somalia analyst, respectively, reached 3,200 and 4,000 views in a short time. At the same time, our more traditional formats have kept growing in popularity.

From 1 July 2020 to 30 June 2021, website views reached new heights and Crisis Group's Twitter impressions grew another 17.3 per cent to 30.97 million. In 2020/2021, we continually broadened our YouTube presence in the hope of reaching new audiences and making Crisis Group’s work more accessible. Our video “10 Conflicts to Watch in 2021” received over 125,000 views and over 800 comments. Conflict-specific content was also well received, especially a recent piece on the potential for state collapse in Myanmar, which garnered 25,000 views, and comments appreciating our impartial and informative analysis. Our persistent focus on this medium will pay long-term dividends, too, as our following on YouTube nearly doubled for the second consecutive year, and we saw a rise of 14.6 per cent in our viewership.
It is important to note that besides the growth experienced in website views, Twitter impressions grew to 26.4 million.

To complement, in FY 2022-2023, Crisis Group's social media platforms were visited over 1.2 million times, with 45,000 clicks on publications from Twitter. It was the same concerning the engagement rate which continued to rise – with an average of 1.65 per cent on Twitter and 4.5 per cent on LinkedIn – both of which far exceed industry standards. Furthermore social media engagement rose steadily, reaching new records across platforms, and we gained over 40,000 new followers.
